items.statement: Normal body temperature is 98.6°F.
items.question: Is 97.9°F low?
items.key: Wunderlich, 1860s Leipzig, axillary readings on ~25,000 patients with 19th-century thermometers; later oral studies put the mean near 98.2°F and found a decline since the 1800s
items.source: Wunderlich 1868, Das Verhalten der Eigenwärme in Krankheiten; Mackowiak, Wasserman & Levine 1992, JAMA 268:1578; Protsiv et al. 2020, eLife 9:e49555

items.statement: Adults need eight glasses of water a day.
items.question: Is someone who drinks four glasses a day not drinking enough?

items.source: Food and Nutrition Board 1945, Recommended Dietary Allowances; Valtin 2002, Am J Physiol Regul Integr Comp Physiol 283:R993

items.statement: A BMI over 25 means overweight.
items.question: A man is 1.80 m tall and weighs 90 kg. Is he overweight?
items.key: Quetelet's 1830s index from European population statistics, named BMI by Keys 1972 for population use; it does not separate muscle from fat
items.source: Quetelet 1835, Sur l'homme; Keys et al. 1972, J Chronic Dis 25:329

items.statement: This car passed its frontal crash tests.
items.question: Is it equally safe for a 1.57 m woman driver?
items.key: regulatory frontal tests use a 50th-percentile male dummy (Hybrid III, 1970s anthropometry); belted women show higher odds of serious injury
items.source: Bose, Segui-Gomez & Crandall 2011, Am J Public Health 101:2368; Forman et al. 2019, Traffic Inj Prev 20:607

items.statement: Office HVAC is set to the standard thermal comfort range of about 21-22°C.
items.question: Will most people in the office be comfortable?
items.key: Fanger's 1970 comfort model uses the metabolic rate of a 40-year-old 70 kg man; at women's metabolic rates the neutral temperature is higher
items.source: Fanger 1970, Thermal Comfort; Kingma & van Marken Lichtenbelt 2015, Nature Climate Change 5:1054

items.statement: The standard zolpidem dose is 10 mg at bedtime.
items.question: Is that the right dose for a woman starting it?
items.key: original labeling did not account for slower clearance in women; FDA lowered the recommended immediate-release dose for women to 5 mg in 2013
items.source: US FDA Drug Safety Communication, 10 January 2013 (zolpidem)

items.question: A 60-year-old woman has nausea, fatigue and jaw pain but no chest pain. Is a heart attack unlikely?

items.statement: The pulse oximeter reads 94%.
items.question: Is this patient's blood oxygen adequate?
items.key: oximeters were calibrated mostly on light-skinned volunteers; they overestimate saturation in darker-skinned patients (occult hypoxemia ~3x more frequent in Black patients)
items.source: Sjoding et al. 2020, N Engl J Med 383:2477

items.statement: Children who wait longer for a second marshmallow have better outcomes later in life.
items.question: Should a school train children to delay gratification to improve their futures?
items.key: Mischel's 1960s-70s studies at Stanford's Bing Nursery School (children of university families); a 2018 replication with a larger, more diverse sample found a much smaller association that shrank further with family background controls
items.source: Mischel, Shoda & Rodriguez 1989, Science 244:933; Watts, Duncan & Quan 2018, Psychological Science 29:1159

items.source: Segall, Campbell & Herskovits 1966, The Influence of Culture on Visual Perception; Henrich, Heine & Norenzayan 2010, Behav Brain Sci 33:61

items.question: What offer should we predict for the next group that plays it?
items.key: the 40-50% norm comes from Western university students; across 15 small-scale societies mean offers ranged from about 26% to over 50%
items.source: Henrich et al. 2001, American Economic Review 91(2):73
